guided_journeys.story_title: The Reaction That Would Not Start
guided_journeys.tagline: Follow one amber substrate across an energy barrier, into an active site, and through repeated catalytic cycles until enzyme action becomes a visible mechanism.

guide.name: Dr. Nia Park
guide.visual: navy field jacket, clear safety glasses, and a compact tablet showing reaction-energy and molecular models
guide.story_job: Nia keeps the workshop geography fixed, asks you to predict the molecular consequence, and names scientific terms only after the defining action is visible.

guided_journeys.premise: A reaction workshop is wasting energy because its molecular jobs have been reduced to labels. The learner must rebuild catalysis by comparing reaction barriers, docking a real substrate at an active site, and watching the same enzyme return to service after product release.
guided_journeys.mission: Follow one reaction from activation-energy barrier to enzyme-substrate binding and catalytic turnover so enzyme action is understood as a reusable molecular mechanism.
guided_journeys.finale: The workshop runs again after the same reaction receives a lower activation-energy pathway, the amber substrate binds a compatible active site through induced fit, products leave, and the unchanged enzyme returns to service. The restored catalyst then unlocks the control wing where enzyme activity can be regulated.

guided_journeys.story_title: The Control Wing That Would Not Hold a Steady Rate
guided_journeys.tagline: Carry one transparent enzyme through eight diagnostic stations and learn to identify why enzyme activity changes from visible molecular evidence.

guide.name: Dr. Nia Park
guide.visual: navy field jacket, clear safety glasses, and a compact tablet showing enzyme shape, reaction-rate, and pathway-control models
guide.story_job: Nia keeps the control-wing geography fixed, changes one variable at a time, asks you to diagnose the cause of each rate change, and names scientific terms after the mechanism is visible.

guided_journeys.premise: The enzyme control wing is producing erratic rates. One reference enzyme is carried through heat, pH, concentration, helper, inhibitor, allosteric, cooperative, and pathway-feedback tests so each regulatory mechanism remains physically distinct.
guided_journeys.mission: Stress and regulate one enzyme system while preserving the difference between altered protein structure, active-site competition, allosteric control, cooperative binding, feedback inhibition, and irreversible loss of function.
guided_journeys.finale: The control wing stabilizes only after every rate change is tied to a distinct physical cause. Environmental stress, saturation, helper requirements, active-site competition, allosteric regulation, cooperative subunits, feedback inhibition, and irreversible inactivation can now be diagnosed from what happens to the enzyme or pathway.

guided_journeys.story_title: The Energy Ledger That Would Not Balance
guided_journeys.tagline: Follow one energy-accounting marker from metabolic pathways through thermodynamic constraints, cellular work, ATP hydrolysis, and ATP regeneration until the hall can account for every transformation.

guide.name: Dr. Nia Park
guide.visual: navy field jacket, clear safety glasses, and a compact tablet showing energy-flow, reaction, and ATP-coupling models
guide.story_job: Nia keeps the energy hall spatially stable, makes each energy transformation visible, asks you to track where usable energy goes, and names scientific terms only after the relationship is clear.

guided_journeys.premise: An energy-exchange hall has lost its accounting system. Metabolic routes, energy forms, thermodynamic constraints, cellular work, and ATP cycling must be reconnected into one lawful energy-flow system.
guided_journeys.mission: Trace how cells transform energy, remain organized while increasing total entropy, couple favorable and unfavorable processes, and continuously regenerate ATP.
guided_journeys.finale: The hall balances only after metabolism is separated into catabolic and anabolic routes, energy forms are tracked under both thermodynamic laws, exergonic processes are coupled to cellular work, ATP hydrolysis is explained through the full reaction, ATP is regenerated continuously, and conserved metabolic logic is recognized across life.
